text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament's Public Accounts Committee rejects a draft statement by its chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa explaining why he wrote a letter to lawyers representing business tycoon Ketan Somaia's Dolphin group.
- The government releases 3,000 bags of maize for distribution to famine-ravaged areas.
- Kenyan police confirm some of $1 million stolen last month from a warehouse in Nairobi are in circulation.
- The World Bank gives the Kenyan government a $50 million loan for rehabilitation of the Nairobi-Mombasa highway.
- A women's development body says it will not support opposition member of parliament Charity Ngilu in her bid for the presidency.
- Police gun down a suspected gangster and recover two pistols and 12 rounds of ammunition in Mombasa.
- Readers Digest South Africa presents a one million shilling cheque to a sugar farmer for his sweepstakes win.
- Business is temporarily halted at the treasury by a bomb scare.

- State House deputy comptroller John Lokorio files a law suit against proprietors of The People weekly for linking him with the president's "kitchen cabinet" and Asian businessmen. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
